weather.tip: 96% chance of rain today — keep an umbrella handy and budget extra commute time, especially near underpasses and low-lying stretches that flood quickly.

around.headline: Drunk techie fires air gun from apartment balcony for 45 minutes, residents and guards take cover
around.summary: A resident allegedly fired an air gun repeatedly from his balcony late into the night, sending neighbours and security guards scrambling for cover before he was subdued. If you ever spot someone firing any kind of gun in a residential area, call 100 immediately rather than confronting them yourself.

around.headline: Green Line metro frequency to be cut tonight (Aug 7) for late-night trials
around.summary: BMRCL will temporarily thin out Green Line frequency on the night of August 7 to run new trainsets ahead of CMRS inspection trials scheduled for August 12–14. Expect longer waits on the Green Line tonight if you're travelling late.

around.headline: Madiwala traffic diversions in effect this week
around.summary: Bengaluru Traffic Police began trial diversions around the Madiwala junction from August 6. If your commute passes through this stretch, plan for detours or extra travel time over the next few days.

around.headline: Nearly half of Bengaluru's 1.03 crore voters flagged for deletion in draft electoral roll
around.summary: The draft Special Intensive Revision (SIR) list marks close to half of Bengaluru's registered voters for possible removal, mostly over non-response or discrepancies. Check your name on the draft roll and file a claim or objection before the correction window closes so you don't lose your vote.

around.headline: Eviction drive clears 230+ encroaching shops at KR Market
around.summary: A Greater Bengaluru Authority demolition drive has cleared over 230 shops it says were encroaching on footpaths near KR Market, some reportedly decades old. If you run a stall or shop near a market footpath, check your documentation now rather than risk a sudden eviction.

around.headline: Zepto, PhysicsWallah among 7 firms fined for 'dark patterns'
around.summary: Consumer authorities fined seven companies, including Zepto and PhysicsWallah, for manipulative 'dark pattern' designs that push users into unwanted purchases or subscriptions. Read cancellation and opt-out screens carefully — a pre-ticked box or a fake urgency timer is often built to trip you up.

events.name: Freedom Habba
events.note: Bengaluru's first Freedom Habba turns Vidhana Soudha into a stage for the city's cultures, with a grand parade and a children's tour of the building — worth planning around if you're free on Independence Day.

events.name: 1,500 Years of Storytelling
events.note: An exhibition tracing Karnataka's hero stones through to Satyajit Ray's drawings — a good pick if you're into art and history.

events.name: 'A Moving Line'
events.note: An exhibition at the Museum of Art & Photography (MAP) traces mural traditions in India that predate manga.

events.name: Strings & Stillness
events.note: Musician Vikram Hazra returns to Bengaluru with a fundraising concert blending music and stillness practices.

street_smart.title: You hear popping sounds from a neighbour's balcony above you, and something lands near your own balcony where your kids are playing. You look up and see a visibly drunk resident firing what looks like an air gun. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Real incident today: a Bengaluru techie allegedly fired an air gun from his apartment balcony for 45 minutes while drunk, sending residents and security guards running for cover before he was subdued (NDTV, The Times of India, Deccan Herald).
street_smart.situation: It's late evening and you're on your balcony with your kids when you hear repeated popping sounds and see something skitter across the floor. Looking up, you spot a neighbour a few floors above, clearly drunk, firing an air gun out over the building. What do you do first?

choices.text: Go up to his flat yourself and confront him about it before he hurts someone.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. He's drunk, armed, and already behaving erratically — walking up to confront him puts you in the direct path of an unpredictable person with a weapon, for no benefit over calling the police, who can act with authority and backup.

choices.text: Shrug it off since it's 'just an air gun', not a real firearm, and go back inside without doing anything.
choices.feedback: Risky. Air guns fire pellets at real speed and have caused serious injuries at close range; combined with alcohol and poor aim from a height, the danger is closer to a real weapon than the name suggests, and ignoring it leaves everyone below at risk.

choices.text: Start filming it on your phone to post online and 'expose' him, before doing anything else.
choices.feedback: Risky. Documentation can help later, but spending the first critical minutes filming instead of getting people to safety and alerting the police delays the response that actually stops the danger.

choices.text: Move everyone away from the balcony and line of fire, call 100, and report the flat number and what you saw.
choices.feedback: Correct. Firing any kind of gun — air gun included — in a residential area recklessly endangers others and can be booked under the Arms Act alongside public-nuisance provisions; police response is faster and safer than any resident trying to intervene directly.

takeaways: Treat air guns as real weapons at close range — get yourself and others out of the line of fire immediately, don't wait to see if it's 'serious'.
Call 100 the moment you see or hear gunfire of any kind in a residential area; don't attempt to confront the person yourself.
Note the flat/floor number, time, and what you observed — it helps police act quickly and supports a formal complaint from your residents' association afterward.

quiz.question: For roughly how long did a drunk resident allegedly fire an air gun from his Bengaluru apartment balcony, as reported today?
quiz.why: Reckless discharge of any gun, including an air gun, in a residential area can be booked under the Arms Act alongside public-nuisance provisions.

quiz.question: In the draft electoral roll released under the SIR exercise, roughly what share of Bengaluru's 1.03 crore voters have been flagged for possible deletion?
quiz.why: Voters flagged in a draft roll aren't automatically removed — they can file a claim or objection during the correction window to stay on the final list.

quiz.question: A trial run for the new Bengaluru–Mangaluru Vande Bharat train, through the Western Ghats section, is set to begin around which date?
quiz.why: The Western Ghats stretch involves steep gradients and curves, which is why trial runs there focus on testing the train's speed and safety systems before passenger service starts.

quiz.question: What is the minimum age required to become a member of India's Lok Sabha?
quiz.why: The minimum age is higher for the Rajya Sabha, India's upper house, where a member must be at least 30 years old.

quiz.question: Which gas do plants primarily absorb from the air to carry out photosynthesis?
quiz.why: Photosynthesis releases oxygen as a by-product, which is why plant-dense green spaces measurably improve local air quality.
